newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - June 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - June 2.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Queensland and New South Wales sides for the second match in the Australian Rugby League State of Origin series are to be named today. Queensland is expected to switch top player Jason Smith to five-eighth in a bid to improve its chances of winning the math to level the series. Page 28.

Super League team the Canberra Raiders have continued their winning streak, defeating the Adelaide Rams 18-14 at Adelaide Oval yesterday. The Raiders fought back from a losing position at half-time and forced the Rams to concede 20 unanswered points. Page 28.

The international Super League competition will be launched in London this week. The new competition, called the World Club Challenge, will see the ten Australian Super League clubs take on their twelve European counterparts over the next three weeks. Page 28.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Australian cricket team is experiencing unexpected difficulties in its Ashes tour of England. Foremost among concerns are the poor performance of captain Mark Taylor, and the lack of exposure given to other team batsmen. Page 25.

New South Wales State of Origin team coach Tom Raudonikis said last night he would be happy for injured players Brad Fittler and Andrew John to train with the team before the second Origin match is held next week. Of the two, Fittler is expected to be named in the New South Wales side today. Page 27.

Super League team the Penrith Panthers have been preparing for the past two weeks for tonight's match against opposing team Canterbury. The long hiatus enjoyed by Penrith is thanks to Super League's scheduling. Page 26.
THE AGE

Australian cricket batsman Greg Blewett scored a century in the match against Derbyshire yesterday. However, he believes he aggravated a knee injury in the process, and has doubts over his fitness for the first Test match Australia plays against England next week. Page 2sport.

The manager of Australian Football League's newest club Port Adelaide, Mick Moylan, is set to sever his ties with the club this week. There has been a breakdown of relations between him and the side following a public disagreement between him and coach John Cahill last week. Page 3sport.

Australian Football League team Essendon, which has been having a disastrous season, is facing the loss of one of its most prized players, Brownlow medallist James Hird. Hird will today have bone scans to determine if he has stress fractures in his feet,if so he will have to be sidelined for over a month. Page 3sport.
THE HERALD SUN

Boxer and former drug addict Vince Phillips yesterday defeated previously unbeaten Australian Kostya Tszyu in the IBF world junior welterweight title in Atlantic City. Tszyu led for most of the fight but was felled by Phillips in the tenth round. Page 94

Australian cyclist Darryn Hill has won his second gold medal at the World Cup being held in Trexlertown, Pennsylvania. He beat defending champion Marty Nothstein in the Kerin Final and in the Olympic sprint final. Page 94.

The Australian Football League is to examine ground level footage of an off-the-ball incident in last Friday's match between Port Adelaide and Carlton. The footage suggests an illegal action by Port Adelaide captain Gavin Wanganeen against Carlton player Greg Williams. Page 93.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Rodney Eade, coach of the Australian Football League team the Sydney Swans, yesterday conceded his team was experiencing a difficult season following the Swans close loss 13 14 (92) to 13 11 (89) to Brisbane yesterday. The loss is the sixth this season for last year's grand finalists. Page 32.

Australian driver Paul Morris has won the second round of the Australian Super Touring Championship motor racing series, extending his lead to 14 points. Fellow competitor David Auger was knocked out of competition by the crash of his Alpha Romeo 155. Page 33.

Australian Rugby Union team the ACT Brumbies are expected to promise to keep together for the 1998 season, increasing expectations that they will soon rank alongside New South Wales and Queensland on the ladder. The Brumbies next game will be against the touring French side on Friday week. Page 34.
-- Sydney Reuters Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
